topics.label: Course introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the cancer lecture series, and the core learning objectives concerning environmental carcinogens and malignancy development.

topics.label: Genetic, environmental, and epidemiological factors in cancer etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises through the interplay of intrinsic genetic mutations, microenvironmental evolution, stochastic factors, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens drive oncogenesis, illustrated in detail by the multi-factorial etiology and pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular mechanisms by which dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage directly or via xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish tumor promoters from initiators, explore how host developmental stage influences tissue susceptibility, and summarize the diverse pathways of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic mutational signature analysis, epidemiological biobanking, and in vivo and in vitro experimental assays used to detect and assess carcinogens.

topics.label: Conclusion and everyday risk-benefit balance
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by summarizing key takeaways and framing carcinogenic exposure within everyday risk-benefit decisions.
